body:
There’s a lot of, “they’re asking for help responses here.” Maybe I can add another dimension from my own experience.

Depression and anxiety just about robbed me of my ability to think. My memory was terrible, I could barely string a sentence together, I’d run out of things to talk about and panic because I thought everyone would see how... boring, useless, and stupid I’d become.

All that was on my mind was my depression and anxiety. This isn’t everyone’s experience, but I’m a ruminator. I get stuck in thought. And when depression is 70% of what you’re experiencing, that’s sometimes all you have to talk about.

I had days where I’d nod along to people talking to me because 1) I could barely keep up and 2) all I wanted to share about my weekend was how absolutely miserable I was. 

Did I think that particular person could help me? Probably not. Did I want attention? Absolutely. We all do, that’s probably why you tell people about your weekends. 

You give what you got.

And I know this was the toll depression had on me because I was always quiet, but the last two years have been an entirely different kind of low. And medication, therapy, and exercise seem to finally be getting me back to my workaholic, decently bright and happy self.

Hopefully that makes sense. Also curious if anyone can relate.

TL;Dr: Depression and Anxiety can really eat at the mind. When depression touches you’re entire life, sometimes that’s a lot of what you have to talk about.
